jurisdiction.authority: Office of the State Superintendent of Education

curriculum.course_title: District of Columbia Mathematics Standards (Common Core), Grades 6-8
curriculum.note: DC adopted the Common Core State Standards verbatim; expectation identifiers are the canonical CCSS codes (e.g., 6.NS.A.1). Unlike Maryland's 2025 MCCRS re-domained framework, DC retains the legacy domain letters RP/NS/EE/G/SP/F.

source_notes: The District of Columbia adopted the Common Core State Standards; OSSE publishes DC standards as the CCSS verbatim.
Expectation identifiers follow the canonical CCSS scheme {grade}.{domain}.{cluster}.{number}; the inventory unit is the top-level standard (lettered sub-parts are not enumerated).
Scope summaries are editorial paraphrases of the CCSS statements; reviewers must compare them with official wording before accepting any mapping.
OSSE adoption was July 2010; implementation began SY 2011-2012 and was complete by SY 2014-2015. The inventory_as_of date is not a standards version or school-year code.

reconciliation.warning: Existing DC6.*/DC7.* seed rows predate the reviewed-taxonomy gate; several are broad domain-level composites (e.g., DC7.SP.PROBABILITY spans all eight 7.SP expectations). Grade 8 has no repository seed rows at all.

classification_legend.standards_mapped: A repository-specific seed row partially overlaps this expectation; this does not mean the mapping is accepted or complete.
classification_legend.reviewed_skill: Independent mathematical approval must cover the exact atomic target and definition.
classification_legend.generator_available: A generator must target the exact reviewed identity; local content is not enough.
classification_legend.validated_practice: Practice must be independently validated against both expectation and skill scope.
classification_legend.assessment_ready: An accepted independent assessment contract must exist.
classification_legend.verified_mastery_evidence: Learner evidence is never inferred from mappings, generators, practice, or tests.
